title: Study to Evaluate the Dose-Dependent Effect of Tirzepatide on Gastric Emptying in Adult Patients With Type 1 Diabetes
official: Open-Label, Non-Randomized, Single-Arm, Multicenter Pilot Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Dose-Dependent Effect of Tirzepatide on Gastric Emptying in Adult Patients With Type 1 Diabetes
summary:
FAITH-T1D/1, exploratory, Phase I, open-label, non-randomized, single-arm, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the dose-dependent effects of tirzepatide on gastric emptying in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight or obesity.

The study will investigate tirzepatide administered once weekly as an adjunct to participants' usual insulin therapy delivered through automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. Tirzepatide will be administered subcutaneously, with gradual dose escalation from 2.5 mg up to 15 mg at four-week intervals, according to clinical tolerability and the protocol-defined dosing schedule. Its use in this population is off-label.

The study follows a longitudinal, within-subject design in which each participant serves as their own control. Gastric emptying will be assessed by gastric emptying scintigraphy using a standardized solid meal at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 16 and 24. The primary objective is to characterize changes in gastric emptying in relation to tirzepatide dose. Secondary and exploratory objectives include evaluating metabolic and glycemic parameters, gastrointestinal symptoms, postprandial glucagon, lipidomic and metabolomic profiles, and the safety and tolerability of treatment. Continuous glucose monitoring and AID system data will also be reviewed throughout the study.

The target is 12 evaluable participants, with a maximum of 14 participants allowed to account for early withdrawals before an evaluable post-baseline assessment. The study includes a screening period, approximately 24 weeks of treatment and follow-up assessments through week 30.

Safety assessments will include treatment-emergent adverse events, gastrointestinal symptoms, hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis, as well as monitoring of tolerability during dose escalation. An independent Data and Safety Monitoring Committee is planned in accordance with the protocol.

The trial will be conducted at two Spanish hospital centers: Hospital Universitario Ramón y Cajal and Hospital Universitari i Politècnic La Fe. The study is exploratory and mechanistic; it is intended to characterize pharmacodynamic effects, estimate within-subject changes and inform the design of future confirmatory studies, rather than establish definitive clinical efficacy.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Written informed consent: Participants must have received information about the study design, objectives, and potential risks and must provide written informed consent to participate.
* Ability to comply with study procedures: Ability and willingness to understand the study, comply with the required procedures, and attend all scheduled visits.
* Age and diagnosis: Age ≥18 years and an established diagnosis of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) for at least 1 year.
* Stable automated insulin delivery (AID) treatment: Stable treatment with an AID system for at least 90 days before the baseline visit (Visit 0), with a commitment to maintain the same mode of insulin delivery and insulin throughout the study.
* Baseline HbA1c: HbA1c between 6.3% and 10.5% at baseline.
* Body mass index and weight stability: BMI ≥25 kg/m², with stable body weight (variation ≤5 kg) during at least the 90 days before inclusion.
* Contraception requirements: Participants with reproductive potential must agree to use effective contraception throughout the study and for at least 6 months after the end of the study. The protocol specifies a highly effective contraceptive method plus a barrier method for participants with reproductive potential.

Exclusion Criteria:

Glycemic control and diabetes

1. Two or more episodes requiring hospitalization for poor glycemic control (hyperglycemia or diabetic ketoacidosis \[DKA\]) during the 180 days before the baseline visit.
2. One or more episodes of severe hypoglycemia requiring assistance from another person during the 90 days before baseline.

   Diabetes complications
3. Active proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or a history of ophthalmologic treatment (photocoagulation, intravitreal injections, or vitrectomy) during the previous 6 months, or anticipated need for such treatment during the 6 months after inclusion.

   Recent cardiovascular disease
4. Cardiovascular events during the 60 days before baseline, including:

   * Acute myocardial infarction.
   * Stroke.
   * Coronary revascularization.
   * Hospitalization for unstable angina.
   * Heart failure. Gastrointestinal disorders and motility
5. Clinically significant gastrointestinal disorders, including diabetic gastroparesis.
6. Previous bariatric surgery.
7. Chronic use of medications that directly affect gastrointestinal motilityRenal function
8. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) below 15 mL/min/1.73 m² at baseline.

   Neoplasms
9. Active malignancy or malignancy in remission for less than 5 years.
10. Personal or first-degree family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2).

    Psychiatric disorders
11. Severe or unstable psychiatric disorders, including uncontrolled major depression, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or other severe psychiatric conditions, or severe mood or anxiety disorders during the previous 2 years.

    Concomitant medications
12. Systemic glucocorticoid use for more than 14 days during the 90 days before baseline, excluding replacement therapy.
13. Use of weight-loss medications or glucose-lowering medications other than insulin during the 90 days before baseline.

    Hypersensitivity
14. Hypersensitivity to tirzepatide or any of its excipients.
